title: Why Was a Strange Signal in Cambridge Called Little Green Men?
description:
In 1967, a short anomaly kept appearing on Cambridge's observation charts. A faster recorder, a second telescope, precise timing and a new source in another part of the sky gradually revealed what kind of signal it was.

LGM was a joking nickname, not a formal announcement of alien civilisation. The oscillation candidates in the first paper of February 1968 and Gold's rotation proposal in May were distinct stages.

Fact checked: 2026-10-16. Participants' recollections and the original papers are identified separately. AI illustrations are narrative aids, not historical photographs or original observation records; modern people are represented by fictional characters rather than likenesses. Drawn waveforms and celestial objects are not presented as original data.

thumbnail.headline:
WHO KEPT
**THE BEAT?**
thumbnail.sub: A mystery on a paper chart

chapters.august-desk: A strange mark returns on the chart
chapters.paper-published: The paper leaves a question open

8748fb3d.text: Bell, a graduate student, unrolls a chart.

a183b99a.text: A short patch looks odd. She checks earlier charts

449bbb4c.text: and finds it again in that part of sky.

b3033eac.text: Is the instrument faulty, or is something really there?

90259fa2.text: Later, they watch a second telescope for the same pulses.

acc6618c.text: Before Christmas, Bell races in before dawn to watch another patch of sky.

2b58a7d7.text: The following May, someone submits a two-page paper about the rhythm.

e205076e.text: Where did the signal nicknamed Little Green Men come from?

e3e46d77.text: Bell and supervisor Hewish speed up the recorder.

0c47ad34.text: The old chart crowds the changes, hiding their shape.

6acf7c94.text: The array sought quasars through changing radio signals.

634a9fab.text: The telescope was new, and the team was learning its quirks.

7ccdf4c3.text: They read charts by eye lest unfamiliar gear hide a signal.

1631f62b.text: Bell alone reads about thirty metres of charts a day.

40de40ee.text: She learns normal radio changes and interference from Earth.

54c3000a.text: But the odd patch fits neither, so she cannot file it with familiar marks.

8d87d7e4.text: By late October, she goes daily to watch that sky pass.

010dcfc2.text: The fast recorder can spread brief changes across the chart.

efd6c54a.text: But for weeks, it records only receiver noise.

05002227.text: Can the fast recorder catch the source seen before?

ae51ed79.text: One day, she attends a talk instead of watching it.

d5b03c7d.text: A routine chart later shows the odd mark returned while she was out.

718638d1.text: On November 28, the fast recorder finally catches it.

ba179597.text: This time the chart shows distinct pulses, one after another.

fdeda684.text: Each pulse is about one and a third seconds after the last.

f58aba8f.text: The rhythm is so regular. Could someone be transmitting it?

37c4b04a.text: Hewish first thinks of man-made radio interference.

b872d2af.text: A nearby transmitter could swamp distant signals in a sensitive telescope.

8e99187b.text: He visits the observatory to see if pulses return.

5315a9f5.text: They do. This is no longer a single misread mark; it keeps happening.

d15db021.text: The team compares each arrival time with the position of the sky.

01625c23.text: It returns with the sky, not at the same clock time each day.

2f1bf500.text: If a machine on Earth made it, that pattern needs explaining.

6de2f659.text: They also test another possibility: human radar reflected by the Moon.

0e6c77f2.text: Their tests rule out that kind of reflection.

8a7445de.text: Even with a matching sky position, they must check the receiving equipment.

cb83227e.text: Would a different system record the same pulses?

f76bb3e1.text: The telescope that initially failed to catch the signal becomes that test.

41b5eb07.text: Bell later recalled that they waited, and the pulses arrived five minutes late.

2ec7abc8.text: They had miscalculated when the source would cross the observing position.

a0f8a979.text: This time, the receiver is independent.

eea8a036.text: It is now hard to blame a fault in the first instrument.

1dfdcacf.text: How far away are those pulses coming from?

2f829cd6.text: Pilkington compares arrival times across radio frequencies.

a88f7286.text: Interstellar matter delays radio waves differently by frequency.

6461789b.text: That difference places the source beyond the Solar System.

e3ef1239.text: So where did the nickname Little Green Men come from?

99a55420.text: Bell says Little Green Men was a joking label she used in her notes.

a995298a.text: A handy nickname did not turn the signal into a message from a civilisation.

aae6c002.text: But Hewish did consider an artificial transmission from a distant planet.

5c699592.text: If that planet orbited a star, precise timing might reveal it.

3d181765.text: Moving toward or away from us would affect the rhythm we receive.

fe82a389.text: The catch: Earth beneath us also orbits the Sun.

27f6aab6.text: He must separate changes caused by Earth from any additional motion.

c9ad2ab4.text: He times pulses closely and tracks period changes.

c0603925.text: The measured change matches Earth's orbital motion.

742fe66c.text: This timing shows no extra motion from the planet he was looking for.

1cf70848.text: This limits an artificial source, but does not identify it.

544d8e26.text: Meanwhile, Bell keeps reading the routine charts as the rolls pile up.

fe66ab8a.text: Before Christmas, she spots a suspect mark in another part of the sky.

aa0353e3.text: With the lab about to close, she searches older charts from that direction.

a24b2bf8.text: They show similar marks. She must catch the predawn observing window.

5d94082f.text: Hours later, Bell arrives to find the receiver frozen by cold.

9d1e006a.text: She later said cold sharply reduced its sensitivity.

b6b8a1c4.text: She flips switches and breathes on the equipment to get it working.

2a075c4c.text: It holds on briefly, pointed toward the patch of sky she needs.

07ceb40b.text: The cold room's new chart shows another pulse train.

ad787132.text: This time, they are about 1.2 seconds apart.

30578f8d.text: The direction and rhythm differ. It cannot just be the first source returning.

7a031219.text: Could more of these signals hide in the charts?

336cd716.text: Bell feels relieved: natural phenomena can occur in groups.

e747682c.text: If all were civilisations, why would they choose the same observing frequency?

dbb65c4a.text: She leaves the chart on Hewish's desk, then goes for Christmas.

22561e92.text: Over the holiday, Hewish tops up the recorder's paper and ink.

e72ed59d.text: She returns to more charts and keeps reading.

9bc5a454.text: This time, one roll holds two strange marks far apart from each other.

9410e2e4.text: It is more than two: the team eventually confirms four sources of this kind.

f0768460.text: With a whole group, what objects are they, and how do they make these beats?

049813c5.text: They publish the first source's observations in Nature on February 24, 1968.

86806d23.text: Researchers worldwide can now compare observations of that source.

bd5c4453.text: But describing it and naming the emitter are separate problems.

3ecdf437.text: The changes come so fast that researchers turn to very dense objects.

facb1101.text: The paper suggests oscillating white dwarfs or neutron stars.

37a80430.text: Both candidates must fit the period and pulse width.

6308da52.text: But they do not yet explain all the pulses seen.

9889f843.text: At the end of the paper, the authors still call for more observations.

9f650d96.text: The next explanation must confront the published periods and pulses.

8f3ddd39.text: If stellar oscillation falls short, what else could make a recurring beat?

fcd9695d.text: Another paper will take a different approach.

b6d2d02b.text: Physicist Thomas Gold's two-page May paper offered rotation, not oscillation.

724570c6.text: For that group, he proposes rotating neutron stars and radio beams.

59adb0ea.text: We see a lighthouse beam only when it turns toward us.

a856f45a.text: On Earth, a receiver records a pulse only when a beam sweeps past us.

2d4ca310.text: When the beam turns away, we hear nothing; the star still spins.

33a0f356.text: The regular gaps on the chart could thus trace a rotation period.

8ac591de.text: Gold also predicted a gradual slowdown; later pulsar observations measured it.

2a37c45e.text: The Little Green Men signal needs no artificial transmitter. Later evidence supports a rotating neutron star whose beam sweeps Earth.

57dd9251.text: The beam's finer physics remains under study.

f28a86d7.text: We can file this case: a natural object's motion can create a precise rhythm.

3ecfc37e.text: When something seems too regular, what evidence would change your mind?

259da0ce.text: Subscribe and follow the records with us to see how strange events unfolded.
